title: Natural sheaf tensor comparison on a localized open site
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings on its open site, and $U$ an open. Let $A$ be its underlying ring sheaf and $V=\operatorname{overFunctor}(A,U)$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. For the sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] there exists a family $e_{M,N}:V(M\otimes_R N)\cong V(M)\otimes_{R|_U}V(N)$ for all sheaves of $A$-modules $M,N$, natural in both variables: for $f:M\to M'$ and $g:N\to N'$, $e_{M',N'}\circ V(f\otimes g)=(V(f)\otimes V(g))\circ e_{M,N}$. No flatness, finiteness or nonemptiness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01CD (modules-lemma-tensor-product-pullback), specialized to open restriction; Tag 03DH (sites-modules-section-localize)

proof.text: Identify each sheaf tensor with the sheafification of its sectionwise presheaf tensor using source tensorObjIsoSheafification. Apply overFunctor to the source comparison.

Compose the localized module-sheafification natural isomorphism, the inverse tensorator of Mathlib strong monoidal presheaf restriction, the tensor of the explicit identity-scalar module isomorphisms, and the inverse target tensorObjIsoSheafification. The identity-scalar comparisons account for the restrictScalars identity included in overFunctor. This constructs the required comparison isomorphism.

Combine naturality of tensorObjIsoSheafification in each variable, naturality of the localized sheafification isomorphism, the presheaf tensorator naturality, and the naturality of the tensor of identity-scalar comparisons. The latter is proved sectionwise and by tensorHom_comp_tensorHom. A generic composition-of-four-squares lemma and the inverse-square cancellation give the required naturality equality.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_open_localized_tensor_natural
    {X : TopCat.{u}} (R : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat.{u})
    (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X) :
    let A := (sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R
    let V := overFunctor.{u} A U
    letI := monoidalCategory R
    letI : MonoidalCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (A.over U)) :=
      monoidalCategory (R.over U)
    ∃ e : ∀ (M N : SheafOfModules.{u} A), V.obj (M ⊗ N) ≅ V.obj M ⊗ V.obj N,
      ∀ (M M' N N' : SheafOfModules.{u} A) (f : M ⟶ M') (g : N ⟶ N'),
        V.map (f ⊗ₘ g) ≫ (e M' N').hom = (e M N).hom ≫ (V.map f ⊗ₘ V.map g)
